title: Health issues caused by information systems
competency: Describe the benefits of health information systems and the health problems caused by unmanaged device use.

keywords.def: A system that quickly produces high-quality health data for planning, review and monitoring.
Pain in the back, neck, chest, arms, shoulders and feet, for example from poor posture during long device use.

en.text: Health information systems quickly produce high-quality data that informs stakeholders for planning, review and monitoring, and improves the whole health system. Mobile devices make it easier to offer and improve care, empower patients with personalised messages, and collect real-time data to use resources well. Figure 1.14 links the Ministry of Health, the Public Health Institute, hospitals, doctors, nurses, laboratories, pharmacies, insurers and patients.

am.text: የጤና መረጃ ሥርዓት ፈጣንና ጥራት ያለው መረጃ ለዕቅድና ክትትል ይሰጣል። ሞባይል ለታካሚዎች መልእክት ይልካል፣ ቅጽበታዊ መረጃም ይሰበስባል።

screens.title: Where does the data go?

opts: Health planners, such as the Ministry of Health, quickly
Nobody; it stays in the tablet

screens.text: A clinic in Afar sends daily malaria case counts by phone to the regional health office. Which benefit does this show?
opts: Real-time data that helps use resources and make decisions

screens.clue: What can the office do with daily counts?

en.text: Unmanaged use of information systems and devices causes sleeping disorders, lack of productivity, loss of attention and stress. It also causes physical problems: musculoskeletal pain in the back, neck, chest, arms, shoulders and feet, vision problems and eye strain, headaches, and obesity from long hours of sitting. Users should learn proper ways to use devices to get the benefits and reduce the harm.

screens.title: Where does it hurt?
screens.text: Tap each part to see how long device use can affect it.
items: Bending over a phone for hours strains the neck.
Slouching in a chair hurts the back.
Long screen time causes eye strain and vision problems.
Headaches can follow long screen use.
Phone use late at night disturbs sleep.
Long hours of sitting can lead to obesity.

paras: Unmanaged use causes sleeping disorders and lack of productivity.

screens.title: Healthy habits
paras: Sit upright; keep the screen at eye level.
20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.

defs: Pain in the back, neck, chest, arms, shoulders and feet, for example from poor posture during long device use.

screens.text: Health-related negative effects of information systems include all EXCEPT
screens.why: Adapting to technology is a positive skill; the others are harms (p.7, p.13).
screens.clue: Which one is a good thing?

screens.title: Physical, or attention and mood?
screens.why: Some harms are to the body; others affect focus, mood and output (p.13).
screens.clue: Can a doctor see it on the body?
What does the body not do while gaming for hours?

screens.ask: With the 20-20-20 rule, 6 hours of screen time needs ___ eye breaks

screens.text: Which change best reduces neck and back pain from phone use?
opts: Hold the phone at eye level and take breaks
Use the phone lying down all day
screens.ans: Hold the phone at eye level and take breaks
screens.why: Good posture and breaks reduce musculoskeletal strain.

screens.text: Meron studies on her phone until 1 a.m., then cannot focus in class and feels stressed. What are her problems, and what is the best fix?
opts: Sleeping disorder and loss of attention; stop screens well before bedtime
Eye strain only; use a bigger phone
screens.ans: Sleeping disorder and loss of attention; stop screens well before bedtime
screens.why: Late screen use causes sleep problems, which lead to loss of attention and stress (p.13).
screens.clue: Start with what happens at 1 a.m.
